# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
## My own mistakes, all recovered, each with the rule it produced

I merged a pull request with its checks still pending, and it broke six CI jobs on a documentation-only change: I had edited two files without regenerating the shipped checksum manifest, so the integrity self-check correctly reported a half-finished update. Wait for checks. The rule is not decoration.

I created a branch inside a repository another live session was working in, and it committed twice underneath me while I worked, leaving their checkout sitting on my branch. I restored it. A shared repository gets a separate clone, never a branch in someone else's working tree.

I edited a live installed skill while a blinded experiment was running, without realising that file sits inside the experiment's own fingerprint scope. Reverted. Before touching anything under ~/.claude, ask what the running experiment measures.

Three times a check returned a confidently wrong answer because my harness asked a different question than I intended: a grep for a machine id when the page renders directory names, a leak check against a temp path when the scrub targets the real home, and a structural diff over fifteen quiet seconds when the drift needed twenty-five. When a repro comes back clean, suspect the harness first.

Once I reported a fix verified when only the secondary guard had been exercised: removing O_NOFOLLOW left the suite green because an explicit symlink check fired first. Defense in depth breaks calibration. Name which guard you targeted.

## The finding that should change how this project is reviewed

The fleet dashboard passed its own opus refuter, then my own independent verification, and a third reviewer found four Criticals in it anyway. One of them, a symlink at the org directory, let the reader escape the store entirely.

The reason is worth more than the four fixes. Every fixture in that suite, including the ones added specifically to cover hostile input, placed a hostile value of the CORRECT TYPE. Raw bytes and huge sizes were covered. A non-string where a string was expected, a number outside float range, and a symlink at or above the org directory were not. Twenty-three tests passed with four Criticals live.

Twice now in this project, a unit has passed its own calibrated tests and been broken in a shape its fixtures could not express. A suite's blind spot is currently the best available predictor of where the next Critical lives.
